theater: 杭州行在皇城與御營司駐地

battle.name: 苗劉兵變
battle.theater: 杭州行在皇城與御營司駐地
battle.brief: 紹興元年二月，南渡未久的宋廷在杭州行在發生禁軍兵變。將校苗海軍、劉延裕以糧餉不公為由夜入皇城，殺內侍、劫持高宗、索械索糧，數日之間被張俊、劉光世所率御營兵平定。全役在宮門與街巷之間進行，並無攻城之事，卡面配重投石車此役並未登場，只能作為同期攻城技術的旁證。

kit.name: 配重投石車
kit.history: 長臂配重把石頭甩過城牆。工程比攻城武器更早決定勝負。

countries: 本役的交戰雙方都出在杭州城內，並無外邦兵馬介入。一方是南宋行在的朝廷：紹興元年二月，高宗駐臨安尚不足兩年，軍政由宰執與樞密院掌握，禁軍分隸殿前司、馬軍司、步軍司三衙與御營司，皇城宿衛由內侍省與殿前司輪值，當值將校多為南渡以來從北方收編、補錄或召募的軍將，軍籍與糧餉都對不上帳。另一方是禁軍將校苗海軍與劉延裕糾集的一批軍士與將佐，另有內侍為內應。這一夥人無國號、無正式編制，也沒有任何外來勢力支持，其訴求限於誅除內侍、交還所掠兵械、補發糧餉與賞賜。兵變一起，衝突的性質便由宮禁內的變亂轉為朝廷與御營大軍的對峙：叛軍佔據皇城與內城一部，朝廷移駕城外，張俊、劉光世所率御營兵自諸路星夜赴援；而金朝大軍同年秋冬已抵江淮的軍情，又使杭州城內每一支兵力的調動都帶著兩層顧慮。
countriesEn: The two sides in this engagement both came from within the city of Hangzhou, and no foreign troops took part. On one side stood the Southern Song court at its temporary capital: in the second month of the first year of Shaoxing, less than two years after the court had settled at Lin'an, military affairs were in the hands of the chancellors and the Privy Council, and the imperial guards were distributed among the three directorates of palace, horse and infantry and the Imperial Camp Command; the night watch of the inner city was held in rotation by the Directorate of Palace Attendants and the palace troops, and most of the officers on duty were men recruited, recorded or picked up from the north after the crossing of the Yangtze, so that neither the muster rolls nor the pay and provisions were in order. On the other side stood a band of soldiers and junior officers mustered by the guard officers Miao Haijun and Liu Yanyu, with palace attendants acting as go-betweens from within. This group had no state name and no regular establishment, and no outside power supported it; their demands were confined to the removal of the eunuchs, the return of the arms they had seized, and the issue of grain and rewards. Once the revolt began, its character changed from a disturbance inside the palace into a confrontation between the court and the Imperial Camp armies: the rebels held part of the inner city, the court moved the emperor outside the walls, and the Imperial Camp troops under Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi hurried in from several circuits by night and day; and since the Jin army had already reached the Huai River in the autumn and winter of the same year, every move of troops inside Hangzhou was loaded with a second layer of anxiety.
people: 高宗趙構是這場變亂中最被動、也最關鍵的一個人。他自靖康二年北狩之後南渡，即位於南京應天府，隨後一路南遷，紹興元年二月以三十出頭的年紀駐在杭州；兵變之夜他被叛軍迎出、劫持於皇城，數日之內遷移數處，隨侍近臣與宮人的秩序全失，這段經歷成為他終身猜忌武將、裁抑內省的深層原因。苗海軍是叛方首要人物，禁軍將校出身，據記載為人桀黠而有勇力，能在禁軍中聚起黨羽；劉延裕地位相近，事起之後反成叛眾所推的盟主，兩人事後皆被擒獲誅殺，部眾或降或散，多被重新編入軍籍。站在朝廷一邊平叛的是張俊與劉光世：張俊時任御營司統制，兵變發後自浙西率部馳援，負責正面進逼；劉光世以御營副使之身分在杭州一帶部署，封鎖城門與要道，斷其內外聯絡。內侍康成是史籍記載中在兵變中被殺的內侍首腦之一，宦官勢力自此一落千丈。此外，御營司中拒絕繳械的將士，以及隨駕百官中主張用招撫而非大攻的臣僚，都在數日之內決定了變亂的結局。
peopleEn: Emperor Gaozong was the most passive and at the same time the most decisive figure in this disturbance. After the northern captivity of 1127 he crossed the Yangtze, took the throne at Nanjing Yingtian, and then moved south in a series of withdrawals; in the second month of the first year of Shaoxing he was a man of a little over thirty holding court in Hangzhou, and on the night of the revolt he was taken out of the inner city and held by the rebels, moving from place to place within a few days while the order of his attendants and his palace collapsed around him. That experience became one of the deepest reasons for his lifelong mistrust of generals and his suppression of the palace eunuch office. Miao Haijun was the leading man of the rebels, a guard officer by origin, described in the records as fierce and cunning and able to gather partisans within the guards. Liu Yanyu stood at his shoulder and in the end was pushed forward by the rebels as their leader; both were taken and put to death afterwards, and their followers either surrendered or scattered, most of them being taken back into the muster. On the court's side stood Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi. Zhang Jun, then commander of the Imperial Camp Command, led troops in from western Zhejiang once the revolt broke out and was responsible for the frontal advance; Liu Guangshi, as deputy commander of the Imperial Camp, deployed around Hangzhou, closed the city gates and the main approaches and cut off the rebels' lines of contact with the outside. The eunuch Kang Cheng is the head of the palace service named in the histories as killed in the revolt, and the authority of the eunuchs fell with him. In addition, the officers of the Imperial Camp who refused to hand over their weapons, and the ministers around the emperor who urged negotiation rather than a general assault, decided the outcome of the disturbance within a few days.
kits: 卡面這件配重投石車，在本役中並沒有出現。苗劉兵變全程發生在皇城、內城與街巷之間，沒有城牆需要轟擊，也沒有攻城與守城的大型工程，它的長臂配重在杭州的巷戰裡找不到任何位置；把它放進這場戰役的裝備體系裡，只能當作同期技術水平的一個旁證。實際上動用到的裝備十分樸素：叛軍一方用刀、劍、槍、戟與弓，破門靠斧、撞木與梯具，奪門用鐵尺、槌，以及火把、猛火油一類的縱火之物；宿衛的殿前司軍士則以長槍與刀盾封住宮門與角樓。朝廷一方能迅速平叛，靠的是御營司的精銳騎兵、禁軍中願意聽令的部隊與城防本身的高牆厚門，而不是任何攻城器械。同期宋軍在北面對金、對西夏的戰線上已常見砲與火箭，《武經總要》所載的霹靂砲、火油櫃、磁石砲一類器具，正是十二世紀東亞的工程技術水平；至於中國式的配重投石車，其文字記載要等到十三世紀蒙古用兵之時才出現，與卡面所標的一一〇〇年、地中海世界同時成熟的配重式樣並不完全相合。
kitsEn: The counterweight trebuchet on the card did not appear in this engagement. The whole of the Miao-Liu revolt was fought in the inner city, the palace and the streets; there was no wall to batter and no large work of siege or defence, and the long counterweighted arm of such a machine had no place in a street fight in Hangzhou. Placed in the equipment system of this campaign, it can only serve as indirect evidence of the technical level of the age. The equipment actually used was plain: the rebels worked with sabres, swords, spears, halberds and bows; when they broke into the gates they used axes, rams and ladders, and when they forced the inner doors they used iron bars, hammers and firebrands together with oil for setting fires. The palace troops on duty, the men of the palace directorate, closed the palace gates and the corner towers with long spears and shields. The court's speed in putting the revolt down came from the picked troops of the Imperial Camp, from those guard units still willing to obey orders, and from the high walls and heavy doors of the city itself, and not from any siege engine. On the northern fronts against Jin and against Western Xia the Song had already used stone and fire projectors, and the devices described in the Wujing Zongyao, the thunder crash bomb, the oil chest and the magnet stone bomb, mark the engineering level of twelfth-century East Asia. As for a Chinese counterweight trebuchet, its written record does not appear until the campaigns of the Mongols in the thirteenth century, and it does not match exactly the form that had matured in the Mediterranean world at the date, 1100, printed on the card.
tactics: 這是一場以夜襲、劫持與政治逼迫為骨幹的宮禁變亂，戰術核心不在會戰而在控制。叛軍利用禁軍值夜的空隙與換班之間的混雜，在夜裡分股殺入皇城，殺死當值內侍，封閉宮門與城門通路，再把高宗迎到預先選定的殿閣，以天子為旗號向御營司索取兵械、糧餉與賞賜，試圖迫使朝廷就範。防守一方的應對同樣以速度為先：急發詔書調御營大軍入城，移駕於皇城之外以絕其挾持之念，封鎖城門要道，切斷叛軍與城外的聯絡，同時遣使入城招撫，明示首惡之外可以免死；等叛軍在城內孤立、糧食斷絕、部下不願再為首惡所用的時候，再分路合擊，於是全役沒有出現像樣的野戰主力交鋒。從兵法上看，叛軍犯了以眾抟單、以人質代軍力、以攻代撫三重毛病；朝廷的贏，則來自把平叛當作治安而非戰爭，寧可讓出宮禁、拖延時間，也不肯在城內大打出手。這與配重投石車時代的常規攻城術正好相反：那一類戰爭靠圍城、掘壕與攻城塔慢慢磨，而這一場只靠幾個時辰內誰先控制城門、誰先把話說到叛軍心裡。
tacticsEn: This was a disturbance of the palace whose skeleton was the night attack, the taking of a hostage and political coercion; the core of its method lay not in a pitched battle but in control. The rebels used the confusion of the guards' night watch and the muddle of the change of shift to enter the inner city in several parties after dark, kill the attendants on duty, close the palace gates and the city approaches, and then bring the emperor to a hall they had chosen beforehand, using the Son of Heaven as their banner to demand arms, grain and rewards from the Imperial Camp Command in the hope of forcing the court to yield. The defence answered with equal speed: edicts were dispatched at once to bring the Imperial Camp armies into the city, the emperor was moved outside the inner city so as to break the rebels' grip, the gates and main roads were sealed, the rebels' contact with the outside was cut, and emissaries were sent in to negotiate, making it plain that all but the ringleaders might be pardoned. Only when the rebels were isolated inside the city, short of food, and their men no longer willing to die for the ringleaders did the court strike in force from several quarters. No proper meeting engagement between main forces took place during the whole affair. Judged by the art of war, the rebels committed three errors at once: taking on a single man with the multitude, using a hostage in place of military force, and offering assault in place of negotiation. The court's victory came from treating the suppression as a matter of public order rather than of war, ready to give up the inner city and to gain time rather than to fight a pitched battle inside the city. This is the opposite of the usual siege of the age of the counterweight trebuchet, which wore a fortress down slowly with blockade, trench and assault tower; this affair turned on which side controlled the gates in the space of a few hours, and on which side first spoke the language the rebels could accept.
data: 可用的數字多為概數，各家記載互有出入。時間上，兵變起於紹興元年二月，即一一二九年二月，地點在杭州皇城與內城，平定亦在同一月之內，據記載大概是數日之間，最後的搜捕在城內街巷完成。叛眾人數史無明確記載，參與者主要是杭州禁軍中的軍士與將校，加上為內應的內侍，人數當在數百至千餘之間，規模不大，卻能直抵宮禁，說明皇城警衛編制本身已被侵蝕。平叛的御營大軍自浙西、淮南兩路星夜赴援，總數以萬計，各家所載多有出入。空間上，臨安羅城周長十餘里，皇城居城東南隅，周圍數里，宮門與樓閣相連，叛軍佔了內城一段，朝廷則退保城外行在。糧餉是本役真正的爭點：南渡之後禁軍膨脹、北方新附軍士待食，內庫與度支一時不濟，據說正因為軍糧屢欠、賞賜不公，軍心才會一觸即發。往後朝廷整軍裁汰冗兵，人數以萬計；同年十月金兵已抵江淮，杭州的告急文書一日數至，這也是朝廷不敢在城內久拖的一個原因。
dataEn: The usable figures are mostly round numbers, and the accounts differ from one another. As to time, the revolt began in the second month of the first year of Shaoxing, that is the second month of 1129, in the inner city and the palace of Hangzhou, and it was put down within the same month; according to the records it took a matter of days, and the last arrests were made in the streets of the city. No history gives a firm number for the rebels. They were mainly soldiers and junior officers of the Hangzhou guards together with palace attendants who acted as go-betweens, and were probably several hundred to a little over a thousand strong; such a small body could still reach the heart of the palace, which shows that the watch system of the inner city had already been eaten into. The Imperial Camp armies that suppressed the revolt hurried in by night from western Zhejiang and from the Huai River circuits, numbering in the tens of thousands, though the various records differ widely. In space, the outer wall of Lin'an ran for more than ten li, the inner city stood in the south-eastern corner of the city and ran for several li, and the palace gates and halls were joined to one another; the rebels held a stretch of the inner city while the court fell back to the temporary palace outside the walls. Grain was the true point at issue. After the crossing of the Yangtze the imperial guards had swollen, the newly attached northern soldiers had to be fed, and neither the treasury nor the finance ministry could meet the demand at short notice; it is said that precisely because military pay and rations were long in arrears and rewards were unfairly distributed that the soldiers' hearts were ready to break out at a touch. Afterwards the court reorganised the army and cut the surplus soldiers, a process counted by the tens of thousands. In the tenth month of the same year the Jin troops had reached the Huai River, and the alarm dispatches from Hangzhou arrived several times a day; this too was a reason why the court dared not drag the matter out inside the city.
cause: 兵變的成因可以分作遠近三層。最遠的一層是靖康之難的餘波：北宋原有的京畿禁軍與邊軍在兩京陷落時潰散大半，健在者或潰於河北，或降於金，或被南渡的宋廷收編，名籍、糧餉、器械都對不上帳，禁軍人數因此暴增而戰力虛浮。第二層是朝廷自身的失度：高宗既不信任北方舊來將領，又倚重內侍監軍、節度內庫，內侍省在皇城宿衛與軍需分派上插手太深，據說軍士所應得的糧餉賞賜常被剋扣，怨氣積在禁軍內部。第三層是眼前的導火線：南渡軍隊久駐江淮，糧道越拉越長，軍中欠餉久矣，而紹興元年正月金人南侵的消息已在江南傳開，將士普遍感到前途無保障；再加上苗海軍、劉延裕這類將校在南渡軍中職位不高、久受冷落，一旦有人敢於先動，散兵游勇式的騷動便可能被點成合謀。所謂匹夫無識之說，用在這裡並不準確：兵變能成，靠的是禁軍內部的編制與警衛漏洞，靠的是內侍為內應，也靠的是朝廷在糧餉與賞罰上的虧欠；這三樣之中任何一樣不在，兩個將校未必拉得起這樣一場事。
causeEn: The causes of the revolt can be divided into a distant, a middle and an immediate layer. The most distant is the aftermath of the Jingkang disaster: the capital guards and frontier armies of the Northern Song were largely scattered when the two capitals fell, and those still alive either broke up in Hebei, or went over to the Jin, or were taken into the service of the court that had crossed the Yangtze, so that the rolls, the pay and the equipment no longer matched, and the size of the guards ballooned while their fighting quality remained hollow. The middle layer is the fault of the court itself: Gaozong trusted neither the old northern generals nor the newly risen officers, and relied on the palace eunuchs to supervise the troops and to control the internal treasuries; the Directorate of Palace Attendants interfered too deeply in the inner watch and in the distribution of military supplies, and it is said that the rations and rewards due to the soldiers were habitually skimmed off, so that the resentment settled inside the guards. The immediate layer is the fuse: the southern armies had been stationed along the Yangtze and the Huai for a long time, the grain route stretched further and further, the troops had long been underpaid, and in the first month of the first year of Shaoxing news of the Jin advance had already spread through the Jiangnan, so that the soldiers were generally persuaded that there was no future before them. Men such as Miao Haijun and Liu Yanyu held low positions in the southern armies and had long been passed over; once somebody dared to move first, a disorderly stir among the rank and file could be lit into a conspiracy. The saying that common men are without understanding does not fit here: the revolt could succeed only because of the gaps in the establishment and the watch of the inner city, because palace attendants served as go-betweens, and because the court had failed in pay and reward. Remove any one of these three and two officers would hardly have been able to raise so much as this.
impact: 兵變平定之後，南宋的軍政格局被重新排了一遍。最直接的變化在宦官：內侍省在變亂中失去內外侍從、宮門鑰匙與部分武備，殺害內侍的同時也失去了信用，其後被大幅裁撤，宮禁警衛改由禁軍與外朝官員分掌，宦官在宋代政治中的分量自此大減，直至南宋亡前都沒有再出現宦官掌兵的局面。其次在軍隊：朝廷自責禁軍宿衛不力，下令整飭軍籍、裁汰冗兵、安置老弱，並把御營司與三衙的權責重新劃分，御營統制更替頻繁，兵柄愈見分散；同時以文臣出任知州知軍、以武人領兵的風氣被有意收緊，這種對將帥的防範心態，日後會在對金作戰最需要大膽用兵的時候屢屢顯出代價。再次在首都：臨安皇城自此按禦變的思路重修，宮門加固、宿衛輪換與警衛層次都作了調整，行在的城防不再是假定太平無事。最後在士氣：兵變本身證明了南渡軍隊的脆弱，也刺激朝廷在隨後數年大力整軍，試圖把雜湊的降附之眾改造成可以依賴的正規軍，這正是其後嶺南、淮西能與金軍周旋的物質基礎。
impactEn: Once the revolt had been put down, the military administration of the Southern Song was rearranged. The first change was in the eunuchs: the Directorate of Palace Attendants lost its attendants, its keys to the palace gates and part of its armed strength in the disturbance, and it lost credit at the same time; it was cut back sharply afterwards, the watch of the inner city was divided between the guards and the civil officials of the outer court, and the weight of the eunuchs in Song politics fell accordingly, never again to the point of an eunuch holding troops in the Southern Song. Second came the army: the court blamed the failure of the night watch, ordered the muster rolls to be put in order, cut surplus soldiers, settled the old and infirm, and redrew the responsibilities of the Imperial Camp Command and the three directorates; Imperial Camp commanders were turned over frequently and military authority was more and more divided. At the same time civil officials were sent out to serve as prefectures and army commanders, and the custom of having military men command armies was deliberately tightened. That mistrust of generals would show its price in the years when the war against Jin most needed bold use of the army. Third came the capital: from then on the Lin'an inner city was rebuilt on the assumption that a mutiny might come, with the gates reinforced and the rotation and layers of the watch adjusted, so that the defence of the temporary capital was no longer planned for a time of peace. Last came morale: the revolt itself proved how fragile the southern armies were, and it pressed the court to spend the next years reorganising them, trying to turn a mixed mass of surrendered and attached men into a regular force that could be relied upon. That was the material basis on which the campaigns in the Lingnan and in western Huai later faced the Jin with some confidence.
result: 紹興元年二月，兵變在杭州平定，苗海軍與劉延裕相繼被擒，事後誅之，餘眾或降或散，多遣散歸伍，無一成建制。變亂的餘波卻長得多：高宗自此對宦官和近侍失了信任，內侍省大為裁減，宮禁宿衛改由禁軍與外朝分掌；朝廷下詔整軍，裁汰冗兵，重新劃分御營司與三衙的權責，並把一批御營統制調離原職。對當時在江南的宋廷而言，這場兵變是一記響亮的警號：首都的門禁與軍隊的糧餉都是空的，北方金兵又在同年秋冬逼近江淮，於是整軍、籌糧、固城三件事被提到最急的位置上。史籍評價謂兵變雖平而失分之重，因為它暴露的不只是幾個軍士的野心，而是南渡之後整個軍制的空殼。往後數十年，禁軍、廂軍與鄉兵的編制屢經更張，御營司與三衙長期並立，而南宋在對金作戰中既要倚重將兵又懼將兵之變的兩難，也就從這次杭州之變開始定型。
resultEn: In the second month of the first year of Shaoxing the revolt was put down in Hangzhou; Miao Haijun and Liu Yanyu were taken in turn and put to death, and the rest of their men either surrendered or dispersed, most of them sent back to the ranks, and not one body of them remained formed into a unit. The consequences, however, ran much further. Gaozong lost his trust in the eunuchs and his personal attendants, the Directorate of Palace Attendants was cut back, and the watch of the inner city was divided between the guards and the civil officials of the outer court. The court issued an edict to reorganise the army, cut surplus soldiers, redrew the division of authority between the Imperial Camp Command and the three directorates, and transferred a number of Imperial Camp commanders from their posts. For the Song court then standing in the Jiangnan, the revolt was a loud warning: the gates of the capital were thin and the grain of the army was empty, while in the autumn and winter of the same year the Jin moved down to the Huai, so that reorganising the army, securing grain and fortifying the city were all pushed to the front of the agenda. The judgement of the histories is that although the revolt was suppressed the loss was heavy, because what it exposed was not the ambition of a few soldiers but the empty shell of the whole military system after the crossing of the Yangtze. Over the following decades the establishment of the guards, the provincial troops and the local militia was revised again and again, the Imperial Camp Command and the three directorates stood side by side for a long time, and the Southern Song's dilemma of having to rely on generals while fearing what generals might do took shape from this mutiny in Hangzhou.
